locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (EE+ H-rearrangement to an unsaturated heteroatom group)

evidence.curator_note: First (alpha) step of eq 4.43: the diethylamine molecular ion, drawn n-ionized at nitrogen (CH3CH2-N(+.)H-CH2CH3), undergoes alpha-cleavage of one ethyl Calpha-Cbeta bond to expel a methyl radical and form the N-ethyl methyleneimmonium ion CH3CH2-N(+)H=CH2 (m/z 58, the M-CH3 base peak of diethylamine). ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arc(s) - a fully drawn 3-fishhook alpha-cleavage. move <1> = the nitrogen odd electron (the '+.' dot, map 8) into the forming N8=C10 pi bond; move <2> = one electron of the breaking C10-C13 (Calpha-Cbeta) sigma bond into that same N8=C10 pi bond (these two barbs land together on the N-CH2 bond, drawn as the 'vv' over N-CH2); move <3> = the other electron of the C10-C13 bond onto the departing methyl carbon (map 13), drawn as the rightmost hook terminating on CH3. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are placed on N in the mapped SMILES ([NH+] with three sigma bonds = N(+.) radical cation), matching the '+.' the book draws over the nitrogen. The retained ethyl (maps 1,5) carries the hydrogen that migrates in the following step.

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (EE+ H-rearrangement, 'rH')

evidence.curator_note: Second step of eq 4.43 (arrow labelled 'rH'): the even-electron N-ethyl immonium ion loses neutral ethylene by a four-centre beta-hydrogen rearrangement, giving CH2=NH2(+) (m/z 30). The book draws the immonium as a folded 4-membered transition state and shows 2 arc(s), both full (two-electron) arrows: arc(i) = the terminal Cbeta-H bonding pair migrating to the nitrogen (drawn 'H -> N(+)', forming the second N-H of the product iminium); arc(ii) = the N8-Calpha(map5) sigma bond electrons dropping into the forming Calpha=Cbeta (C1=C5) pi bond (drawn as the downward arc from the N-CH2 bond into the H2C-CH2 bond). ENCODING NOTE: only arc(ii) is transcribed as electron_move <1> (bond 5-8 -> bond 1-5); arc(i) terminates on the migrating hydrogen, which the validator's RDKit parse folds into implicit-H counts (atom-mapped H atoms are stripped in this build), so the C-H/N-H bond change is NOT separately encodable. The H migration is instead reflected in the heavy-atom implicit-H counts (C1 CH3 -> =CH2, N8 =NH -> =NH2+). No arc is omitted from the drawn figure's heavy-atom skeleton; the single encoded move exactly matches drawn arc(ii). PRINTED INTENSITY: none - this page prints no percentages or spectrum; the text states m/z 30 is 'the second largest peak in the spectrum of diethylamine' (a qualitative statement, not a printed %), so relative_intensity is omitted.

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_43_ (alpha-cleavage) and IMS_4_43_rH (H-rearrangement). VERIFIED bond-by-bond against their DFS. IMS_4_43_ '[C]1(H..)[C]5(H..)[N+.]8(H)[C]10(H..)[C]13(H...)>>[C]1..[C]5..[N+]8(H){=}[C]10.. . [C.]13...' breaks the Calpha-Cbeta bond C10-C13, forms the N8=C10 pi bond and moves the nitrogen radical into that pi bond while C13 leaves as .CH3 - identical to step_alpha_cleavage; the cleaved C10-C13 bond IS incident to C10, the atom that forms the new N=C double bond, so the rule geometry is correct (no mismatch). IMS_4_43_rH '[C]1(H3)[C]5(H2)[N+]8(H){=}[C]10(H2)>>[C]1(H2){=}[C]5(H2) . [N+]8(H)(H){=}[C]10(H2)' transfers H4 from C1 to N8, forms C1=C5 (ethylene) and breaks the N8-C5 bond, leaving CH2=NH2+ - the same net change as step_h_rearrangement; the cleaved N8-C5 bond is incident to C5, which forms the new C1=C5 pi bond, so this rule is also correctly encoded (no mismatch). Both rules localise charge/radical exactly as the book draws (N-ionized molecular ion; even-electron immonium). Computed monoisotopic m/z (electron-corrected cations, RDKit ExactMolWt) are curator-derived: the page prints no numeric intensities.
